description: Content creation and cross-platform distribution system -- CreatorOS core differentiator: universal composer, platform integrations, cross-posting, content calendar, editing studio, stories, newsletters, analytics, and AI content assistance

domain_summary.role_in_product: Content distribution is the primary differentiator that separates CreatorOS from point solutions. It is the reason a creator chooses CreatorOS over Buffer + Gumroad + Teachable + Discord. Every other module (community, courses, marketplace) produces content that flows through this distribution system.
domain_summary.eos_boundary: EOS handles business operations (client management, revenue tracking, agent orchestration). CreatorOS handles content creation, distribution, community, and consumer experience. Content analytics lives in CreatorOS. Business analytics lives in EOS. Revenue attribution spans both via UMH substrate.
domain_summary.competitive_position: Buffer/Hootsuite are scheduling tools. CreatorOS is a full creator business stack where scheduling is one module. The gap: Buffer cannot sell courses, host communities, or run UGC campaigns. CreatorOS can, and the distribution engine ties it all together.

cross_posting.description: The core mechanism that fulfills the 'post once, publish everywhere' promise. Takes composed content and distributes it to selected platforms with per-platform adaptation.

steps.name: compose
steps.description: Creator writes content in universal composer. Selects target platforms. Attaches media.

steps.name: adapt
steps.description: Platform adapter layer generates per-platform variants. Truncates text, adjusts media, formats hashtags, splits threads. Shows preview per platform.
steps.ai_role: Suggest platform-specific copy improvements, optimal hashtag sets, and engagement-maximizing format choices

steps.name: review
steps.description: Creator reviews per-platform previews. Can override any adaptation. Can add platform-specific additions (first comment on Instagram, alt text, etc.).

steps.name: schedule_or_publish
steps.description: Creator chooses immediate publish or scheduled time. Can set different times per platform. AI suggests optimal times per platform based on audience activity.
steps.ai_role: Recommend optimal posting times per platform based on historical engagement data

steps.name: distribute
steps.description: Server-side job dispatches to each platform API. Handles retries on failure. Records per-platform status (success/pending/failed/rate_limited).
reliability_requirements: Retry with exponential backoff on transient failures (429, 500, 502, 503)
Dead letter queue for permanently failed posts
Per-platform circuit breaker to avoid cascading failures
Webhook or polling for async publish confirmation (some platforms are async)

steps.name: confirm
steps.description: Creator sees per-platform publish status. Can retry failed platforms. Gets notification when all platforms confirm.

steps.name: track
steps.description: Per-platform engagement metrics aggregated over time. Unified analytics view shows cross-platform performance of a single piece of content.

format_adaptation.description: Rules engine that transforms universal content into platform-specific formats

adaptation_rules.description: If content exceeds platform character limit, truncate intelligently at sentence boundary. Append '...' and link to full post on CreatorOS.
adaptation_rules.ai_role: Rewrite to fit limit while preserving key message (not just truncate)

adaptation_rules.description: If content exceeds single-post limit on thread-capable platforms (Twitter, Threads), split into numbered thread. Maintain narrative coherence across parts.
Convert media to platform-accepted formats. Resize images. Transcode video. Generate thumbnails.
Suggest or auto-crop media to platform-optimal aspect ratios. Instagram: 1:1 or 4:5. Pinterest: 2:3. TikTok/Reels: 9:16.
Adjust hashtag count and selection per platform best practices. Instagram: up to 30, research-backed. Twitter: 2-3 max. LinkedIn: 3-5.
Instagram: move link to bio + 'link in bio' CTA. Twitter: inline link with card preview. LinkedIn: link in comment (algorithm prefers no links in post). Pinterest: destination URL field.
Convert @mentions to platform-specific format. Verify handle exists on target platform. Warn if mentioned user not found.

scheduling.description: Schedule posts for future publication across platforms
features: Per-platform scheduling (different times for different platforms)
Queue system (add to queue, auto-publish at next optimal slot)
Bulk scheduling (upload CSV or import from content plan)
server_side_requirements: Reliable job scheduler (not cron -- needs sub-minute precision and failure handling)
Per-platform rate limit tracking and queuing
Missed schedule recovery (if server was down at scheduled time)

open_questions.question: Editing studio priority: build, buy, or embed? CapCut-like editing is a major engineering investment vs licensing a third-party SDK.
Newsletter as content type or separate module? Should newsletters be composable in the universal composer alongside social posts, or have a dedicated editor?
Scheduling infrastructure: what job scheduler for sub-minute precision? Options include BullMQ (Redis-based), pg-boss (Postgres-based), or Temporal (workflow engine).

implementation_debt.description: God files (routes.ts 53KB, storage.ts 104KB) must be split before content distribution can be built. Adding 30+ new endpoints to a 53KB file is technically possible but operationally reckless.
Auth is broken (comparePasswords returns true for ALL passwords). Content distribution involves OAuth tokens for external platforms -- cannot store sensitive tokens behind broken auth.
No test infrastructure. Content distribution involves complex state machines (scheduling, retry, multi-platform coordination). Building without tests guarantees production failures.
UMH projection code (projections/creatoros/integration/, 1099 lines) is DORMANT. AI content features depend on UMH substrate integration which exists in code but is not activated.
Posts table lacks scheduling fields (scheduled_at, published_at, status). Schema migration required before any scheduling feature can be built.
No connected_accounts table in schema. All cross-posting depends on OAuth connections to external platforms which have no storage surface.

build_sequence_recommendation.description: Recommended build order for content distribution features, accounting for dependencies and blockers
build_sequence_recommendation.note: This is a professional recommendation, not an operator decision. Build sequence is OPEN_QUESTION_OPERATOR_DECISION_REQUIRED.

phases.name: Foundation (unblocks everything)
items: Fix auth (Clerk migration) -- P0 security, unblocks OAuth token storage
Split god files (routes.ts, storage.ts) -- P1, unblocks all new feature development
Add test infrastructure (vitest) -- P1, unblocks safe development
Schema migration: add scheduling fields to posts, create connected_accounts table

items: Multistreaming (if operator approves for product scope)
